About me

Mechanical engineering student with research experience in materials testing and atmospheric science.

I'm studying mechanical engineering at West Texas A&M University, with a minor in mathematics, and I graduate in May 2027. Most of my work is hands-on: experimental mechanics and materials testing. Right now, I'm focused on fabricating silicone composites embedded with soft inclusions and testing them on the UniVert S tensile tester to see how those inclusions, and their volume fraction, change the stiffness of the material. This area of research will help us understand and model soft-tissue injuries and design soft robotics.

Before that, I spent three years working in an environmental research group, focused mainly on atmospheric science research. I ran an ice-nucleation chamber remotely at the ARM site on Alaska's North Slope and used the data to connect wildfire smoke to ice formation in clouds. In the summer of 2024, I interned at Pacific Northwest National Laboratory, where I set up the lab's new PINE chamber from scratch and ran more than 100 freezing experiments between −10 °C and −60 °C.

Outside of research, I'm Vice Chair of our ASME student chapter and a lab teaching assistant in the College of Engineering. I also served as a counselor at our engineering camp, where I loved contributing to younger students' first hands-on experiences with engineering, and I've enjoyed teaching air-quality lessons to kids in schools around Canyon and Amarillo.

You can read more about my work on the research and projects pages. If you'd like to talk about internships, research, or a collaboration, I'd love to hear from you.

Research

My undergraduate research at West Texas A&M, from atmospheric ice nucleation to soft-material mechanics.

Soft materialsSept 2025 – present

Elastomechanical Effects in Solid–Liquid Composites

Investigating how liquid inclusions affect the stiffness and deformation of soft silicone composites, with applications in soft-tissue injury modeling and soft robotics.

  • Fabricating silicone–glycerin specimens across matrix stiffnesses, including Ecoflex 00-30 and 00-50.
  • Parametric studies of inclusion geometry and volume fraction using the UniVert S tensile testing system.
  • Literature review of solid–liquid composite mechanics and biofidelic materials.
Atmospheric scienceSept 2023 – Aug 2025

Atmospheric Ice Formation Impacted by Wildfires

Observational study linking wildfire smoke to cloud-ice formation on Alaska's North Slope, funded by a Presidential Research Grant through the Kilgore Research Program.

  • Remotely operated the PINE chamber at the North Slope of Alaska ARM site to quantify ice-nucleating particle concentrations.
  • Computed HYSPLIT back-trajectories and correlated elevated INP events with wildfire activity.
  • Identified significant seasonal and post-wildfire trends across three sites using Python; presented at the departmental research symposium.
Atmospheric scienceSept 2023 – Dec 2024

Cryogenic Freezing Experiments on Atmospheric Aerosols

Characterized ice activation temperatures of field-collected aerosol samples in the WT-CRAFT cryogenic chamber.

  • Performed immersion and condensation freezing experiments on filter samples from multiple field sites.
  • Trained four undergraduate researchers in sample preparation and safe chamber operation.
  • Diagnosed and resolved temperature, pressure, and sensor faults to maintain uptime.

Design & Simulation Projects

Things I've designed, built, modeled, and simulated.

Design & fabrication

Sheep Laparoscopy Table

A welded steel surgical table for laparoscopic procedures in sheep, with a scissor-lift base for height adjustment and a cradle on top to hold and position the animal during the procedure.

Fire & smoke modeling

Building Fire Simulation in CFAST

Modeled fire and smoke spread through a multi-room building using NIST's CFAST zone fire model, visualizing the fire source and flow through doors and vents in Smokeview.

CAD & drafting

Miniature Race Car: CAD Model and Engineering Drawing

Designed a miniature race car body in Autodesk Inventor and documented it in a fully dimensioned engineering drawing with plan, side, front, and section views, then rendered the finished model.
